key_insight: A large bilingual radiology dataset can train a single vision-language model to generate reports, answer questions, and localize findings without manual spatial annotations.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support radiology workflows by improving open-ended question answering while adding spatially verifiable outputs for CT and MR images.
method: Built RefRad2D from 1.2M German/English CT and MR image-text pairs from clinical practice.
Auto-generated VQA and grounding subsets using LLM-based curation plus automated segmentation.
Trained RadGrounder for report generation, VQA, and grounding via bounding boxes or segmentation.
evidence_signal: On external benchmarks such as Slake and VQA-RAD, RadGrounder was competitive with specialized medical VLMs, and adding clinical data improved open-ended VQA without hurting language quality.
watch_item: The dataset and grounding labels are automatically derived, so real-world performance may depend on the quality of the curation and segmentation pipeline.
paper_title: Scalable Training of Spatially Grounded 2D Vision-Language Models for Radiology
